verses.zh: 王住在自己宫中，耶和华使他安靖，不被四围的仇敌扰乱。
verses.en: The king settled into his palace,[NOTE:1] for the Lord gave him relief[NOTE:2] from all his enemies on all sides.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “house” (also in the following verse).
Or “rest.”
The translation understands the disjunctive clause in v. 1b as circumstantial-causal.

verses.zh: 那时，王对先知拿单说：「看哪，我住在香柏木的宫中，　神的约柜反在幔子里。」
verses.en: The king said to Nathan the prophet, “Look! I am living in a palace made from cedar, while the ark of God sits in the middle of a tent.”

verses.zh: 拿单对王说：「你可以照你的心意而行，因为耶和华与你同在。」
verses.en: Nathan replied to the king, “You should go[NOTE:1] and do whatever you have in mind,[NOTE:2] for the Lord is with you.”
notes: Several medieval Hebrew mss and the Syriac Peshitta lack this word.
Heb “all that is in your heart.”

verses.zh: 当夜，耶和华的话临到拿单说：
verses.en: That night the Lord’s message came to Nathan,

verses.zh: 「你去告诉我仆人大卫，说耶和华如此说：『你岂可建造殿宇给我居住呢？
verses.en: “Go, tell my servant David, ‘This is what the Lord has said: Do you really intend to build a house for me to live in?

verses.zh: 自从我领以色列人出埃及直到今日，我未曾住过殿宇，常在会幕和帐幕中行走。
verses.en: I have not lived in a house from the time I brought the Israelites up from Egypt to the present day. Instead, I was traveling with them and living in a tent.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in a tent and in a dwelling.” The expression is a hendiadys, using two terms to express one idea.

verses.zh: 凡我同以色列人所走的地方，我何曾向以色列一支派的士师，就是我吩咐牧养我民以色列的说：你们为何不给我建造香柏木的殿宇呢？』
verses.en: Wherever I moved among all the Israelites, I did not say[NOTE:1] to any of their leaders[NOTE:2] whom I appointed to care for[NOTE:3] my people Israel, “Why have you not built me a house made from cedar?”’
notes: Heb “Did I speak a word?” In the Hebrew text the statement is phrased as a rhetorical question.
Heb “tribes of Israel” (so KJV, NASB, NCV), but the parallel passage in 1 Chr 17:6 has “judges of Israel.”
Heb “whom I commanded to shepherd” (so NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 「现在，你要告诉我仆人大卫，说万军之耶和华如此说：『我从羊圈中将你召来，叫你不再跟从羊群，立你作我民以色列的君。
verses.en: “So now, say this to my servant David, ‘This is what the Lord of Heaven’s Armies has said: I took you from the pasture and from your work as a shepherd[NOTE:1] to make you leader of my people Israel.
notes: Heb “and from after the sheep.”

verses.zh: 你无论往哪里去，我常与你同在，剪除你的一切仇敌。我必使你得大名，好像世上大大有名的人一样。
verses.en: I was with you wherever you went, and I defeated[NOTE:1] all your enemies before you. Now I will make you as famous as the great men of the earth.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “cut off.”
Heb “and I will make for you a great name like the name of the great ones who are in the earth.”

verses.zh: 我必为我民以色列选定一个地方，栽培他们，使他们住自己的地方，不再迁移；凶恶之子也不像从前扰害他们，
verses.en: I will establish a place for my people Israel and settle[NOTE:1] them there; they will live there and not be disturbed[NOTE:2] anymore. Violent men[NOTE:3] will not oppress them again, as they did in the beginning
notes: Heb “plant.”
Heb “shaken.”
Heb “the sons of violence.”

verses.zh: 并不像我命士师治理我民以色列的时候一样。我必使你安靖，不被一切仇敌扰乱，并且我―耶和华应许你，必为你建立家室。
verses.en: and during the time when I appointed judges to lead my people Israel. Instead, I will give you relief[NOTE:1] from all your enemies. The Lord declares[NOTE:2] to you that he himself[NOTE:3] will build a dynastic house[NOTE:4] for you.
notes: Or “rest.”

In the Hebrew text the verb is apparently perfect with vav consecutive, which would normally suggest a future sense (“he will declare”; so the LXX, ἀπαγγελεῖ [apangelei]). But the context seems instead to call for a present or past nuance (“he declares” or “he has declared”). The synoptic passage in 1 Chr 17:10 has וָאַגִּד (vaʾaggid, “and I declared”). The construction used in 2 Sam 7:11 highlights this important statement.
Heb “the Lord.”

Heb “house,” but used here in a metaphorical sense, referring to a royal dynasty. Here the Lord’s use of the word plays off the literal sense that David had in mind as he contemplated building a temple for the Lord. To reflect this in the English translation the adjective “dynastic” has been supplied.

verses.zh: 你寿数满足、与你列祖同睡的时候，我必使你的后裔接续你的位；我也必坚定他的国。
verses.en: When the time comes for you to die,[NOTE:1] I will raise up your descendant, one of your own sons, to succeed you,[NOTE:2] and I will establish his kingdom.
notes: Heb, “when your days are full and you lie down with your ancestors.”
Heb “your seed after you who comes out from your insides.”

verses.zh: 他必为我的名建造殿宇；我必坚定他的国位，直到永远。
verses.en: He will build a house for my name, and I will make his dynasty permanent.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and I will establish the throne of his kingdom permanently.”

verses.zh: 我要作他的父，他要作我的子；他若犯了罪，我必用人的杖责打他，用人的鞭责罚他。
verses.en: I will become his father and he will become my son. When he sins, I will correct him with the rod of men and with wounds inflicted by human beings.

verses.zh: 但我的慈爱仍不离开他，像离开在你面前所废弃的扫罗一样。
verses.en: But my loyal love will not be removed from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.

verses.zh: 你的家和你的国必在我（原文是你）面前永远坚立。你的国位也必坚定，直到永远。』」
verses.en: Your house and your kingdom will stand before me[NOTE:1] permanently; your dynasty[NOTE:2] will be permanent.’”
notes: Heb “before you.” A few medieval Hebrew mss read instead “before me,” which makes better sense contextually. (See also the LXX and the Syriac Peshitta.) The MT reading is probably the result of dittography (note the כ [kaf] at the beginning of the next form), with the extra כ then being interpreted as a pronominal suffix.
Heb “throne.”

verses.zh: 拿单就按这一切话，照这默示，告诉大卫。
verses.en: Nathan told David all these words that were revealed to him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “according to all these words and according to all this revelation, so Nathan said to David.”

verses.zh: 于是大卫王进去，坐在耶和华面前，说：「主耶和华啊，我是谁？我的家算甚么？你竟使我到这地步呢？
verses.en: King David went in, sat before the Lord, and said, “Who am I, O Sovereign Lord, and what is my family,[NOTE:1] that you should have brought me to this point?
notes: Heb “house.”

verses.zh: 主耶和华啊，这在你眼中还看为小，又应许你仆人的家至于久远。主耶和华啊，这岂是人所常遇的事吗？
verses.en: And you didn’t stop there, O Lord God! You have also spoken about the future of your servant’s family.[NOTE:1] Is this your usual way of dealing with men,[NOTE:2] O Sovereign Lord?
notes: Heb “and this was small in your eyes, O Lord God, so you spoke concerning the house of your servant for a distance.”

Heb “and this [is] the law of man”; KJV “is this the manner of man, O Lord God?”; NAB “this too you have shown to man”; NRSV “May this be instruction for the people, O Lord God!” This part of the verse is very enigmatic; no completely satisfying solution has yet been suggested. The present translation tries to make sense of the MT by understanding the phrase as a question that underscores the uniqueness of God’s dealings with David as described here. The parallel passage in 1 Chr 17:17 reads differently (see the note there).

verses.zh: 主耶和华啊，我还有何言可以对你说呢？因为你知道你的仆人。
verses.en: What more can David say to you? You have given your servant special recognition,[NOTE:1] O Sovereign Lord!
notes: Heb “and you know your servant.” The verb here refers to recognizing another in a special way and giving them special treatment (see 1 Chr 17:18). Some English versions take this to refer to the Lord’s knowledge of David himself: CEV “you know my thoughts”; NLT “know what I am really like.”

verses.zh: 你行这大事使仆人知道，是因你所应许的话，也是照你的心意。
verses.en: For the sake of your promise and according to your purpose[NOTE:1] you have done this great thing in order to reveal it to your servant.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for the sake of your word and according to your heart.”
Heb “to make known, your servant.”

verses.zh: 主耶和华啊，你本为大，照我们耳中听见，没有可比你的；除你以外再无　神。
verses.en: Therefore you are great, O Sovereign Lord, for there is none like you. There is no God besides you! What we have heard is true.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in all which we heard with our ears.” The phrase translated “in all” בְּכֹל (bekhol) should probably be emended to “according to all” כְּכֹל (kekhol).

verses.zh: 世上有何民能比你的民以色列呢？你从埃及救赎他们作自己的子民，又在你赎出来的民面前行大而可畏的事，驱逐列邦人和他们的　神，显出你的大名。
verses.en: Who is like your people, Israel, a unique nation[NOTE:1] on the earth? Their God[NOTE:2] went[NOTE:3] to claim[NOTE:4] a nation for himself and to make a name for himself! You did great and awesome acts for your land,[NOTE:5] before your people whom you delivered for yourself from the Egyptian empire and its gods.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “a nation, one.”
Heb “whose God” or “because God.” In the Hebrew text this clause is subordinated to what precedes. The clauses are separated in the translation for stylistic reasons.
The verb is plural in Hebrew, agreeing grammatically with the divine name, which is a plural of degree.
Heb “redeem.”
Heb “and to do for you [plural form] the great [thing] and awesome [things] for your land.”
Heb “from Egypt, nations and their gods.” The LXX has “nations and tents,” which reflects a mistaken metathesis of letters in אֶלֹהָיו (ʾelohayv, “its gods”) and אֹהָלָיו (ʾohalayv, “its tents”).

verses.zh: 你曾坚立你的民以色列作你的子民，直到永远；你―耶和华也作了他们的　神。
verses.en: You made Israel your very own people for all time.[NOTE:1] You, O Lord, became their God.
notes: Heb “and you established for yourself your people Israel for yourself for a people permanently.”

verses.zh: 「耶和华　神啊，你所应许仆人和仆人家的话，求你坚定，直到永远；照你所说的而行。
verses.en: So now, O Lord God, make this promise you have made about your servant and his family a permanent reality.[NOTE:1] Do as you promised,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and now, O Lord God, the word which you spoke concerning your servant and concerning his house, establish permanently.”
Heb “as you have spoken.”

verses.zh: 愿人永远尊你的名为大，说：『万军之耶和华是治理以色列的　神。』这样，你仆人大卫的家必在你面前坚立。
verses.en: so you may gain lasting fame,[NOTE:1] as people say,[NOTE:2] ‘The Lord of Heaven’s Armies is God over Israel!’ The dynasty[NOTE:3] of your servant David will be established before you,
notes: Heb “and your name might be great permanently.” Following the imperative in v. 23b, the prefixed verbal form with vav conjunctive indicates purpose/result.
Heb “saying.” The words “as people” are supplied in the translation for clarification and stylistic reasons.
Heb “the house.” See the note on “dynastic house” in the following verse.

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华―以色列的　神啊，因你启示你的仆人说：『我必为你建立家室』，所以仆人大胆向你如此祈祷。
verses.en: for you, O Lord of Heaven’s Armies, the God of Israel, have told[NOTE:1] your servant, ‘I will build you a dynastic house.’[NOTE:2] That is why your servant has had the courage[NOTE:3] to pray this prayer to you.
notes: Heb “have uncovered the ear of.”
Heb “a house.” This maintains the wordplay from v. 11 (see the note on the word “house” there) and is continued in v. 29.
Heb “has found his heart.”

verses.zh: 「主耶和华啊，惟有你是　神。你的话是真实的；你也应许将这福气赐给仆人。
verses.en: Now, O Sovereign Lord, you are the true God.[NOTE:1] May your words prove to be true![NOTE:2] You have made this good promise to your servant.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the God.” The article indicates uniqueness here.
The translation understands the prefixed verb form as a jussive, indicating David’s wish/prayer. Another option is to take the form as an imperfect and translate “your words are true.”
Heb “and you have spoken to your servant this good thing.”

verses.zh: 现在求你赐福与仆人的家，可以永存在你面前。主耶和华啊，这是你所应许的。愿你永远赐福与仆人的家！」
verses.en: Now be willing to bless your servant’s dynasty[NOTE:1] so that it may stand permanently before you, for you, O Sovereign Lord, have spoken. By your blessing may your servant’s dynasty be blessed from now on into the future!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “house” (again later in this verse). See the note on “dynastic house” in v. 27.
Or “permanently”; cf. NLT “it is an eternal blessing.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is a crucial Messianic passage. This chapter continues to specify the origin of YHWH's special coming king.

- from Abraham ‒ Gen. 12:1-3

- from the tribe of Judah ‒ Gen. 49:10

- from the family of Jesse/David ‒ 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17

- from a virgin ‒ Isa. 7:14 (Matt. 1:23, LXX)

- comes during the fourth kingdom (i.e., Rome) ‒ Dan. 2:34-35

- born in Bethlehem (David's hometown) ‒ Micah 5:2

- This chapter is a word play on "house."

- a temple for YHWH, vv. 3,5,6,7,13,27

- a dynasty for David, vv. 9,11,12,16,18,19,26,27,29 (twice)

- David's palace, v. 1

- YHWH removed Saul for his covenant disobedience but he promises David he will not do that to him or his descendants
(v. 13) but will correct them as a Father (v. 14).

- Since the kingdom of Judah was

- exiled by Babylon (i.e., king and royal house)

- finally destroyed by Rome
the "eternity" factor (vv. 16,24,25,29) must refer to the Messiah who was from Abraham,
Judah, David, born during the Roman Empire.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

- Notice the variety in Israel's Deity's name.

- God (Elohim), vv. 2,23,24,26,28; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

- Lord (YHWH), vv. 2,3,4,5,11 (twice),18,24; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

- Lord of Hosts, vv. 8,26,27; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord OF HOSTS

- Lord God (Adon YHWH), vv. 18,19 (twice), 20,22,25,28,29

- God of Israel (Adon), v. 27 (cf. 1 Chr. 17:24)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 7:1-3

1Now it came about when the king lived in his house, and the Lord
had given him rest on every side from all his enemies, 2that the king said to Nathan the prophet,
"See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells within tent curtains." 3Nathan said
to the king, "Go, do all that is in your mind, for the Lord is with you."

7:1 "in his house" This refers to David's palace which Hiram of Tyre helped build (cf. 2 Sam. 5:11-12).

▣ "the Lord had given him rest on every side from all his enemies" This is
an aspect of YHWH's covenant promise (cf. vv. 9,11; i.e., "the Lord is with you,"
v. 3, cf. Deut. 28:7). This peace showed YHWH's presence and blessing as well as David's covenant obedience. Most covenants are conditional
("if. . .then"; i.e., 1 Kgs. 9:4-7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

7:2 "Nathan" As David used the High Priest to know YHWH's will (i.e., Urim and Thummim), he also used prophets
to hear from YHWH. The two main prophets during the period were

- Nathan, cf. 2 Sam. 7:12; 1 Kings 1

- Gad, cf. 1 Sam. 22:5; 2 Sam. 24:11-13,14,18,19

▣ "the ark of God" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT.

▣ "dwells within tent curtains" It is uncertain the shape of David's new tent (2 Sam. 6:17;
1 Chr. 15:1,3; 16:1). Many scholars assume it was a combination of

- the tabernacle of the wilderness (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF THE WILDERNESS.)

- the larger structure mentioned in 1 Samuel 1

YHWH designed His first tabernacle to be portable to go with Israel during the Exodus and Conquest
(vv. 6-7), but now Jerusalem had become its permanent home. This was the special place that YHWH Himself chose
to dwell (see Deut. 12:5,11,21; 14:23,24; 16:6,11; 26:2).

Not only did the "tent" dwell (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal PERFECT) but YHWH Himself
dwelt there, in the holy of holies, above the wings of the cherubim on the lid of the ark.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

▣ "tent curtains" The tabernacle in the wilderness is called by two names.

- "tent" (BDB 13) ‒ 2 Sam. 6:17; 1 Chr. 15:1; 16:1; 2 Chr. 1:4

- "curtains" (BDB 438; NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 542) ‒ Exod. 26:1,2,8; Num. 4:25; here; 1 Chr. 17:1; Jer. 4:20; 10:2

I am not sure if there is an intended difference or just literary variety.

The problem has to do with which tent is being referred to here. It seems that the tabernacle of the
wilderness, first set up in the Promised Land at Shiloh (cf. Josh. 18:1; 19:51; 1 Sam. 2:22), was later moved to Gibeon,
where it stayed during David's life (cf. 1 Chr. 16:39-40; 2 Chr. 1:2-6) and was not moved to Jerusalem until Solomon's
reign (cf. 2 Chr. 1:3-4,13).

7:3 "Go, do all that is in your mind, for the Lord is with you" These are two
Qal IMPERATIVES. However, Nathan spoke presumptuously from his own opinion without
prayer and consultation with YHWH. We must remember "revelation" is from YHWH (v. 4), not the mind and heart of
man, even a called and gifted man!

For "mind," which is literally "heart" (BDB 523), see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 7:4-7

4But in the same night the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
5"Go and say to My servant David, 'Thus says the Lord, "Are you the
one who should build Me a house to dwell in? 6For I have not dwelt in a house since the day I brought
up the sons of Israel from Egypt, even to this day; but I have been moving about in a tent, even in a tabernacle.
7Wherever I have gone with all the sons of Israel, did I speak a word with one of the tribes of Israel,
which I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, 'Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?'"'

7:5 "My servant David" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT.

▣ "Are you the one who. . ." This was the key question. Should David, a man of war (cf. 1 Chr. 22:8; 28:3),
build YHWH's temple/house or should his son, a man of peace?

The UBS Handbook for Translators, p. 252, mentions that both pronouns "you" and "Me" are emphasized.

7:7 This is similar to the statement in 1 Kgs. 8:16 (i.e., Solomon's dedication of the Temple).

- here, it says "one of the tribes of Israel"

- in 1 Kings "a city out of all the tribes of Israel"

However, the parallel in 1 Chr. 17:6 has "Judges." The word "Judges" (BDB 1047,
שׁפט is very close to "tribes" (BDB 986,

שׁבטי). Judges fits the context much better.

▣ "which I commanded to shepherd My people" This seems to refer to the different leaders from different tribes.

- Moses ‒ Levi (cf. Num. 27:17)

- Aaron ‒ Levi

- Joshua ‒ Ephraim

- Judges ‒ many different tribes (v. 11 and 1 Chr. 17:6 parallel)

- Samuel ‒ Levi (maybe)

- Saul ‒ Benjamin (cf. 2 Sam. 5:2)

- David ‒ Judah

However, if it should be "judges" (see note above), it would simply refer to "leaders" of different types (cf. v. 11).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 7:8-17

8"Now therefore, thus you shall say to My servant David, 'Thus says the
Lord of hosts, "I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep,
to be ruler over My people Israel. 9I have been with you wherever you have gone and
have cut off all your enemies from before you; and I will make you a great name, like the names of
the great men who are on the earth. 10I will also appoint a place for My people Israel
and will plant them, that they may live in their own place and not be disturbed again, nor will the
wicked afflict them any more as formerly, 11even from the day that I commanded
judges to be over My people Israel; and I will give you rest from all your enemies. The
Lord also declares to you that the Lord
will make a house for you. 12When your days are complete and you lie down with your
fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, who will come forth from you, and I will establish his
kingdom. 13He shall build a house for My name, and I will establish the throne of his
kingdom forever. 14I will be a father to him and he will be a son to Me; when he commits
iniquity, I will correct him with the rod of men and the strokes of the sons of men, 15but
My lovingkindness shall not depart from him, as I took it away from Saul, whom I removed from before
you. 16Your house and your kingdom shall endure before Me forever; your throne shall be
established forever."'" 17In accordance with all these words and all this vision, so Nathan
spoke to David.

7:8 "the Lord of hosts" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord OF HOSTS.

▣ "I took you from the pasture" David was the younger, most unlikely choice for king (cf. 1 Samuel 16).
There are several ways YHWH shows His sovereign choice.

- several of the wives of the Patriarchs were barren

- often the firstborn was not the leader of the family

7:9 This wording is similar to YHWH's promise to Abraham in Gen. 12:1-3. As a matter of fact, it is a
continuation of those promises.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

7:10 YHWH is promising a home land. This promise is the focus of the OT, while the promise to David's seed
and an eternal kingdom is the focus of the NT (i.e., Micah 5:2-5).

Canaan is often called YHWH's land. Notice the land given to Israel was the only land bridge between
the two major powers of the ANE.

- Egypt

- Mesopotamia

Only God could keep them in the land (i.e., supernatural acts). Also notice the things mentioned in
vv. 8-10 are "grace" acts. The OT is as much a reflection and revealer of the grace of God as is the NT. It is
difficult theologically to balance

- the grace acts and promises of YHWH

- with the covenant obedience (i.e., "if. . .then") of the Mosaic covenant; see D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and
Pruning Hooks, "Conditional or Unconditional?" pp. 44-47

They are both true, yet #1 must have priority.

▣ "I will plant them" This VERB (BDB 642, KB 694, Qal PERFECT
with waw, the FIRST PERSON emphasizes YHWH's action) is agricultural imagery, but it is used of
YHWH's actions for Israel in Exod. 15:17; Ps. 44:2; 80:8,15; Isa. 5:2,7; Jer. 2:21; 11:17; 12:2; 24:6; 31:28; 32:41; 42:10;
Ezek. 17:23; Amos 9:15. The vine often symbolizes Israel. YHWH is the husbandman. The ground, the plants, the crop are His!

▣ "and not be disturbed again" Israel was "disturbed" by "the wicked" because of her covenant
disobedience (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28). Verse 10 implies a new day of covenant obedience
(cf. Deut. 30:1,15,19). The promises of YHWH to Israel were always conditional. There is tension here because
YHWH's ultimate purpose was the redemption of all people. On one level, His purposes are sure, but on another
level the blessings are conditional on individual and corporate choices!

7:18-29 This is David's prayer of thanks for YHWH's wonderful promises about his descendants. The parallel
is in 1 Chr. 17:16-27.

7:18 "sat before the Lord" This must have been somewhere in the new tent.

The problem occurs when we try to interpret David's actions in light of the Mosaic covenant. Did David

- offer sacrifices

- bless the people

- go into the inner shrine

These were all actions limited to Levitical priests.

There is also the unusual VERB "sat" (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal
IMPERFECT with waw). No priest ever "sat" in the inner shrine. It may be an idiom of
remaining a long time. If "sat" is literal it may be a gesture of humility or contrition.

that the nations saw only YHWH's judgment on His own people (cf. Galatians 3).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is this chapter so theologically significant?

- How does 2 Samuel 7 differ from 1 Chronicles 17?

- How does one explain the promise of an eternal kingdom when one sees the Assyrian and Babylonian exiles
and the Roman destruction of the Temple?

- Why is v. 15 so important?

- Does v. 22 assert full monotheism?

- Explain the word "forever" in this context.
